literal: "I will be ruined," let one's own mind know, if, deviating from neutrality, one does things that are not right.
translation: Let a person's own mind realize, "I will be ruined," the moment they deviate from neutrality and commit unjust deeds.
modern: ஒருவன் நடுவுநிலைமையிலிருந்து விலகி, அறமல்லாத செயல்களைச் செய்ய நினைத்தால், 'நான் அழியப் போகிறேன்' என்பதை அவனுடைய நெஞ்சமே அறிந்து கொள்ளட்டும்.
explanation: This couplet warns of the self-destructive nature of losing one's impartiality. The poet states that if a person deviates from neutrality (நடுவு ஒரீஇ) and performs unjust actions (அல்ல செயின்), their own conscience or mind (தன் நெஞ்சம்) should immediately recognize (அறிக) that ruin is imminent ("கெடுவல் யான்"). The key word 'ஒரீஇ' means abandoning or deviating from, and 'அல்ல' refers to deeds that are not righteous or fair. Thus, the inner conscience acts as an early warning system, foreseeing the inevitable downfall that follows unfairness.
